notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).
No official HDMS website was found (the project page lived on the Max-Planck-Institut fuer Kernphysik site and no capture could be read).

Two set-ups under one name: the prototype with natural Ge crystals (March 1998 to July 1999) and the final set-up with an enriched 73Ge inner crystal (from August 2000); both are phases of this record.
A conference paper of May 2006 is the latest source read that has HDMS in operation; its end is therefore recorded as 'completed' with low confidence and no end date.
The 2005 Phys. Lett. B 609, 226 paper (spin-dependent WIMP-neutron limits from HDMS) could not be read; the limit is recorded from the 2006 paper that cites it.
Placement: The hall is not named in the sources read; the Atlas holds three LNGS hall records that share one approximate point (site:lngs-hall-b is the one the DAMA records use).

physics_goals.quote: HDMS should be able to test the DAMA evidence region within about three years
physics_goals.value: Search for WIMP dark matter with a low-background germanium detector, designed to test the evidence region of DAMA

summary.plain: HDMS, the Heidelberg Dark Matter Search, was a germanium experiment under the Gran Sasso mountain in Italy. A small germanium crystal sat inside a larger one that vetoed stray radiation, so it could look for dark matter particles recoiling off germanium nuclei. It reported limits on how strongly such particles can interact.
summary.technical: Two concentric HPGe detectors in one cryostat: a small p-type inner crystal (202 g in the prototype; later replaced by a crystal of enriched 73Ge, which adds spin-dependent sensitivity) is the WIMP target; a 2.1 kg well-type outer crystal is the anticoincidence shield. Prototype at LNGS March 1998 to July 1999 (natural Ge; 9.9 kg d, 2 keV threshold); final setup from August 2000 (5 keV threshold; 26.74 kg d in 2002; 85.48 kg d in a spin-dependent WIMP-neutron analysis cited in 2006).
